title: The Reformation
key_facts: Triggered by Martin Luther’s 95 Theses in 1517 challenging indulgences and Church authority
Rapid spread through pamphlets and vernacular bibles aided by the printing press
Fragmentation of Western Christianity into various Protestant traditions
causes: Abuses and perceived corruption within the late medieval Catholic Church
Humanist critiques and calls to return to scriptural sources
Political interests of princes and cities seeking autonomy from Rome
outcome: Formation of Protestant churches (Lutheran, Reformed, Anglican)
Catholic Counter-Reformation (Council of Trent) and new religious orders
Religious conflicts culminating in the Thirty Years’ War; Peace of Westphalia (1648)
impacts: Reshaped European politics, education, and confessional identities
Strengthened state authority over churches in many regions
Expanded literacy and debate through widespread print culture
